claims.text: Maintaining the build platform at approximately 500°C throughout laser powder bed fusion will reduce thermal gradients in CoCrFeMnNi components.
Reducing thermal gradients through platform pre-heating will improve dimensional precision relative to fabrication on a room-temperature substrate.
Reducing thermal gradients through platform pre-heating will improve mechanical integrity relative to fabrication on a room-temperature substrate.
Platform pre-heating will produce fewer solidification defects than fabrication on a room-temperature substrate.
Platform pre-heating will lower residual stresses relative to fabrication on a room-temperature substrate.
Room-temperature-substrate laser powder bed fusion of CoCrFeMnNi typically produces significant thermal gradients.
Room-temperature-substrate laser powder bed fusion of CoCrFeMnNi typically produces residual stresses.
Room-temperature-substrate laser powder bed fusion of CoCrFeMnNi typically produces porosity.
Room-temperature-substrate laser powder bed fusion of CoCrFeMnNi typically produces inter-layer delamination.
Elevating the substrate temperature lowers the cooling rate.
Elevating the substrate temperature moderates thermal shock.
The lower cooling rate and moderated thermal shock produce a more uniform microstructure.
The lower cooling rate and moderated thermal shock produce a more equiaxed microstructure.
The proposed thermal modification reduces porosity.
The proposed thermal modification reduces cracking.
Reduced defects and residual stresses enhance dimensional precision.
Reduced defects and residual stresses enhance mechanical integrity.
Pre-heated builds will exhibit fewer inter-layer delaminations than room-temperature-substrate builds.
Excessive or poorly controlled pre-heating may cause undesired grain growth or microstructural coarsening.
Pre-heating-induced grain coarsening may negatively affect mechanical properties.
